guideTitle: Best Mini Split Air Conditioners Under $1000 (2026)
metaDescription: Five 9,000 and 12,000 BTU mini split heat pumps at or under $1,000 from ROVSUN, Rellytech, Upstreman, Albott and Costway, compared on SEER2 and install.
expertTake: The Rellytech 12,000 BTU 115V mini split is the pick at this cap because its stated 12,000 BTU cooling and 12,500 BTU heating, four fan speeds and plug-friendly 115 volt supply fit a bedroom or small apartment. The ROVSUN 9,000 BTU is the value choice with a 28 dB mute mode and Wi-Fi. Anyone planning to install without a licensed technician should read the refrigerant and permit rules in their jurisdiction first.
introParagraphs: A ductless mini split pairs a wall-mounted indoor head with an outdoor compressor, joined by a thin line set. It cools and heats one room or one zone without ductwork, and an inverter compressor runs at partial speed instead of cycling, which is why a good one is quieter and cheaper to run than a window unit.

Prices move, and the $1000 cap used here reflects live listing prices when this guide was updated. At this cap the units are single-zone heat pumps in the 9,000 to 12,000 BTU range, so the guide concentrates on the numbers and install realities that decide whether one will work in your home: SEER2, voltage, low-temperature heating and who is allowed to connect the refrigerant.

products.name: Rellytech 12,000 BTU 19 SEER2 Mini Split AC and Heat Pump, 115V

specList.label: Modes
specList.value: Cool, heat, fan, dry with four fan speeds

products.description:
The Rellytech lists 12,000 BTU of cooling and 12,500 BTU of heating, a 19 SEER2 efficiency rating and a 115 volt supply, which many homes already have in a convenient place. It offers four modes, cool, heat, fan and dry, a smart eco function and four fan speeds with a customizable airflow pattern. Stating both the cooling and heating capacities is the useful part, since many listings quote only one.

A 115 volt unit draws a higher current than a 230 volt unit of the same capacity, but it avoids the need for a 240 volt circuit, which can be a real saving in a small apartment. Next to the Upstreman 230V, it uses the common household voltage and states its heating output. Set beside the ROVSUN 9,000 BTU, it has more capacity and fits a larger room.

A 12,000 BTU unit is a good match for about 500 to 600 square feet, though the listing may suggest more. Plan the install carefully: the line set, the condensate drain and the electrical connection each have requirements. Clean the indoor filters every month and keep the outdoor coil free of debris. Mount the indoor head high on an interior wall with a clear throw of at least a few feet in front, since a head hidden behind furniture or a curtain short circuits its own airflow. If the unit will serve a room with a door that stays closed, leave a gap under the door so air can return, which stops the room from becoming pressurized and lopsided in temperature.
products.bestFor: A bedroom, studio or small apartment where 115V power is the easy path.
pros: States both 12,000 cooling and 12,500 heating BTU
Four fan speeds and eco mode
cons: Professional refrigerant work is still advisable

products.name: ROVSUN 9,000 BTU Wi-Fi Mini Split AC and Heater, 20 SEER2, 115V
products.description:
The ROVSUN is a 9,000 BTU inverter mini split with Wi-Fi control, a 115 volt supply and a stated efficiency of 20 SEER2. The listing quotes noise as low as 28 dB in mute mode and a temperature range of 61 to 88 degrees Fahrenheit. A smaller 9,000 BTU size suits a bedroom or a small office.

A 28 dB figure is a manufacturer claim in the quietest mode and will rise at higher fan speeds, but the direction is right for sleeping. The listing lists both 19 SEER and 20 SEER2, which is a reminder to read the rating label on the actual unit. Measured against the Rellytech 12,000 BTU, it is smaller and costs less, but it cannot handle a larger space. Against the Costway, it adds Wi-Fi.

Size carefully, since an oversized unit short cycles and an undersized one runs constantly. Hire a qualified installer for the refrigerant connections. Clean the filters monthly. The wide setting range suits people who like to hold a steady temperature overnight, and an eco or sleep mode that nudges the setpoint can trim running time further.
products.bestFor: Small bedrooms and offices where quiet and app control matter.
cons: Noise claim is for the quietest mode
Two efficiency numbers on the listing

products.name: Upstreman 12,000 BTU 20 SEER2 230V Mini Split AC and Heating System
products.description:
The Upstreman is a 12,000 BTU unit on 230 volts with a 20 SEER2 rating, R32 refrigerant and Wi-Fi control through the Smart Life app. Inverter technology adjusts compressor speed to hold temperature. R32 is a refrigerant with a lower global warming potential than R410A and is used in smaller charges.

A 230 volt supply draws roughly half the current of a 115 volt unit of the same capacity, which means thinner wire and a smaller breaker, but it requires a 240 volt circuit. Next to the Rellytech, it has a higher SEER2 rating and a more efficient electrical profile at the cost of that circuit. Set beside the Albott, it has a higher SEER2 number.

Have a licensed electrician install the 240 volt circuit and a qualified technician handle the line set. Keep the indoor head level so condensate drains properly. Clean the filter monthly. Over a long cooling season, the lower current draw also puts less strain on the home wiring and avoids dimming lights when the compressor starts, which is a real difference in older houses. The outdoor unit should sit on a level pad with space on all sides and a clear path for air, because a coil boxed in by shrubs loses capacity quickly.
products.bestFor: Homes with a 230V circuit available and a desire for the higher SEER2.

products.name: Albott 12,000 BTU SEER2 18 Inverter Mini Split AC and Heat Pump, 115V
products.description:
The Albott is a 12,000 BTU inverter heat pump with a SEER2 rating of 18, a 115 volt supply and four modes: cooling, heating, dehumidifying and fan. According to the listing, it operates in extreme conditions from 5 degrees Fahrenheit. A low-temperature rating matters if you plan to use it for winter heat.

Heat pump output falls as outdoor temperature drops, and a 5 degree rating means the unit can run in cold weather but not at its full rated heat. Measured against the Rellytech, its SEER2 is lower but its cold operating range is stated. Against the Upstreman, it uses 115 volts, so no special circuit is needed.

In a very cold climate, keep a backup heat source for the coldest nights. Check the condensate drain path and keep it from freezing outside. Clean the filters monthly. Outdoor units in snowy regions benefit from a raised stand and a hood so snow and ice do not block the coil, and a heat pump in defrost mode will shed meltwater that can refreeze on the pad. Learn the defrost cycle's sounds early, because the unit briefly stops heating and may puff steam, which is normal.
products.bestFor: Cool-winter homes that want a stated low-temperature operating limit.
pros: Operates down to 5F per the listing
cons: SEER2 18 is lower than the 20 units
Heat output falls in cold weather

products.name: COSTWAY 12,000 BTU 20 SEER2 Mini Split AC and Heater, 115V, AHRI Certified

specList.label: Modes
specList.value: Auto, cool, dry, heat and fan

products.description:
The Costway is a 12,000 BTU, 1 ton heat pump with a 20 SEER2 rating, a 115 volt supply and an AHRI certification. It is pre-charged with refrigerant, which simplifies the install, and offers five modes, auto, cool, dry, heat and fan. A remote lets you control it from the bed or the sofa.

AHRI certification means the capacity and efficiency numbers have been verified by an industry program, which is more than a plain label claim. Next to the Rellytech, it lists a certification where the Rellytech lists capacities. Set beside the Albott, it has a higher SEER2 number.

A pre-charged system still needs correct installation and, in most places, a licensed technician for refrigerant work. Follow local code on permits. Clean the filters monthly. Keep the manual and the AHRI paperwork with the unit, because a verified rating helps with utility rebates in some regions and gives you something concrete to show an inspector. The remote is simple but lacks scheduling, so set a sleep timer rather than leaving it running all night.
products.bestFor: Buyers who value an AHRI-listed unit and a simple remote.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A baseline is about 20 BTU per square foot of living space at an 8 foot ceiling, so 9,000 BTU suits roughly 450 square feet and 12,000 BTU about 600, even when listings claim 750. Strong sun adds ten percent, and a kitchen adds 4,000 BTU. Oversizing makes a unit short cycle and leaves the room clammy. Whole-house sizing uses a Manual J load calculation. For a single room, a rough check is to measure the floor area, add ten percent for sun and compare with the SEER-rated capacity, remembering that a slightly small inverter unit running steadily beats a large one that cycles. Rooms with high ceilings, large west windows or poor insulation need a size up, and an energy audit finds the cheap fixes.

SEER2 is the seasonal efficiency rating under the newer test procedure, and a higher number means lower running cost. The listings here range from 18 on the Albott to 20 on the ROVSUN, Upstreman and Costway. The difference between 18 and 20 is small compared with the difference between a mini split and a window unit. Use SEER2 to compare within a size class.

A 115 volt unit uses a common household supply but draws more current, while a 230 volt unit draws about half as much and needs a 240 volt circuit. The Upstreman uses 230 volts and the others use 115. Check the nameplate amps and the breaker size before you buy. A new circuit adds cost.

A heat pump moves heat from outdoors in, and its output drops as the outdoor temperature falls toward freezing. The Albott lists operation down to 5 degrees Fahrenheit and the Rellytech states 12,500 BTU of heating, but neither delivers full output in deep cold. In a very cold climate, plan for backup heat. Check the manufacturer's low-ambient output table. Many budget units publish only a minimum operating temperature and not the capacity at that temperature, so a unit that runs at 5 degrees may produce only a third of its rated heat. If your design temperature is below 20 degrees, ask the seller for the capacity at 17 degrees and 5 degrees before you buy.

Quiet mini splits advertise 23 to 30 dB indoors, as the ROVSUN's 28 dB mute mode does. These figures are measured at the lowest fan speed in a lab, so real noise is higher. The outdoor unit adds its own sound. Place it away from bedroom windows.

DIY mini splits use pre-charged line sets with quick-connect fittings so no vacuum pump or refrigerant handling is needed, and line set length is limited by the charge. Standard systems require a licensed technician for refrigerant handling and vacuuming in most jurisdictions. Check local code and permit rules before you start. A bad install ruins efficiency. Common faults include a line set that is kinked, insulation that is crushed, a drain with no slope and a wall bracket that is not level, and each one shows up as a symptom: noise, sweating, leaks or poor cooling. A good installer pressure tests the connections, pulls a vacuum when the system calls for it and documents the charge, so ask about those steps before you hire.

howToChoose.note: Choose 230V if you can add the circuit cheaply, and 115V for the simplest path.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A low indoor noise claim, a sleep mode and a unit sized close to the room. Place the indoor head away from the pillow.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The ROVSUN is the quietest claim, and the Rellytech is the more capable choice.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a cold-climate heat pump with a published low-ambient output table, a multi-zone system or a licensed installation. Higher tiers add dependable cold weather heat.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You cool one bedroom, in which case a single-zone 9,000 BTU unit is enough.

maintenance.why: A clogged filter cuts airflow and efficiency. Rinse and dry.
Dust and leaves cut efficiency. Rinse gently with a hose.
A blocked drain leaks inside. Clear it with air or a thin brush.
Damaged insulation causes sweating and loss. Repair it.
Refrigerant and electrical checks need a technician.

faq.q: Can I install a mini split myself?
faq.a: Pre-charged line sets with quick connects exist for DIY. Most jurisdictions still require a licensed technician for refrigerant handling and permits, so check local rules.
It buys single-zone 9,000 and 12,000 BTU inverter heat pumps. The cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

faq.q: How big a room will 12,000 BTU cool?
faq.a: About 500 to 600 square feet in typical conditions. Listings that claim 750 are generous.

faq.q: Does a mini split heat in winter?
faq.a: Yes, as a heat pump, but output falls as outdoor temperature drops. A very cold climate needs backup heat.

faq.q: How long do mini splits last?
faq.a: Twelve to twenty years with maintenance. Cheaper units may sit at the lower end of that range, and units in coastal air or dusty yards need extra coil cleaning to reach it. An annual professional check is the cheapest way to find a slow refrigerant leak before it kills the compressor.
It draws less current, but needs a 240 volt circuit. 115V is simpler where wiring is limited.
